standard_prerequisites.use: Presents the stack as a quotient of a scheme by a groupoid so that normalizations may be glued.

standard_prerequisites.name: The construction of the normalization of a scheme and its behaviour under smooth morphisms
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 10271-10295) as cross-chapter pointers
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the integral morphism from the normalized presentation.

core_obligations: Choose the presentation: use the preparation lemma to obtain a smooth presentation of the stack such that the hypotheses hold, and write the stack as the quotient of the presentation by its groupoid (proof lines 10248-10270)

Normalize the presentation and descend: normalize the presentation, verify that the normalization is stable under the two morphisms of the groupoid, and descend it to an integral morphism of algebraic stacks over the original stack (proof lines 10271-10295)

Identify the smooth base change: for a smooth morphism from a scheme to the stack, the resulting fibre product is the normalization of that scheme by the compatibility between normalization and smooth base change (proof lines 10296-10303)
proof_roadmap: 由 prepare-normalization 取满足条件的展示，把 X 写成 [U/R]。
对 U 取正规化 U^ν；由正规化与光滑基变换的相容性验证 U^ν 在 R 的两支投影下相容 ⇒ 下降为 X 上的整态射 X^ν → X。
对任意概型 U → X 光滑，纤维积 X^ν ×_X U 由相容性恰是 U 的正规化。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a stack satisfying the hypotheses of the preparation lemma has an integral morphism from its normalization which restricts, after any smooth morphism from a scheme, to the normalization of that scheme (author lemma at source lines 10235-10246, label lemma-normalization). The proof (source lines 10248-10304) chooses the prepared presentation, normalizes the presentation, verifies that the normalization is compatible with the groupoid and descends it, and identifies the smooth base change with the normalization of the test scheme (proof lines 10248-10303). The descent of the normalization through the groupoid is the substance. H3.
